newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares slip on inflation worries.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares slip on inflation worries.

text.p: Norwegian shares plunged on concern about interest rates overseas and higher-than-expected inflation forecasts at home on Wednesday, dealers said.
Oslo's Total index fell 1.01 percent to 1,078.50 points in healthy trade worth 886 million crowns.

The central bank projected inflation at between 2.75 percent and 3.0 percent this year, up from 2.5 percent in a similar report three months ago. This contrasted with a Statistics Office forecast last month of 1.8 percent for this year.
Dealers said some foreign investors had lost faith in the Norwegian stock market.
"The foreigners are negative. They dominate among the sellers, while at the same time there are few buyers," one said.
Losses were suffered across the board with blue chip shares such as Norsk Hydro, Kvaerner, Aker RGI and Orkla all losing ground.

But Aker Maritime gained 2.50 crowns to finish at 108 crowns the day after an industry source said the offshore subcontractor is expected to win a 1.3 billion crown contract for the construction of the topside for Norsk Hydro's Oseberg gas platform.
